info.name: TetraFi API
info.description: Generated from the TetraFi integrator specification. Set baseUrl, apiKey and signingSecret in your local collection variables. Start with GET /api/v1/assets. Replace angle-bracket placeholders with real values before sending other requests; review each write rather than running the entire collection. Never share populated credentials.

exec: // Never retain headers from an earlier signed send when signing is turned off.
// Resolve variables ONCE, including dynamic variables, before hashing and sending.
if (!parts) throw new Error('Set baseUrl to an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL');
// Encode explicitly and disable subsequent transport encoding, so the signed
// target is exactly what is sent. Keep already percent-encoded bytes unchanged.
if (pm.request.body.mode !== 'raw') throw new Error('Signing supports raw request bodies only');
// JSON comments are not valid API input and Postman would strip them AFTER
// signing. Refuse them rather than signing bytes different from the wire.
if (!/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i.test(secret)) throw new Error('signingSecret must contain 64 hexadecimal characters');
// A write needs a nonce accepted once per key: a new random UUID on every send.
if (nonce !== null && !/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,128}$/.test(nonce)) throw new Error('Could not generate an X-Nonce');
const canonical = [timestamp, ...(nonce === null ? [] : [nonce]), method, pathWithQuery, digest].join('\n');
if (nonce !== null) pm.request.headers.upsert({ key: 'X-Nonce', value: nonce });

`details.reason` `ASSET_FILTER_INCOMPLETE`).

request.description:
Read up to 20 resources in one request

Run up to 20 published JSON GETs under one authentication, with each read's own permissions. Signed requests cannot be batched. Guide: [reference/conventions#read-several-resources-at-once](https://tetrafi.mintlify.app/reference/conventions#read-several-resources-at-once). The answer is `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. If an operation's declared related-read allowance cannot fit, or it exceeds that allowance, its item answers `429 BATCH_RELATED_READ_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, not partial values. An item that cannot dispatch to its named operation answers `BATCH_UNKNOWN_ROUTE`.

request.description:
Exchange client credentials for a token

RFC 6749 client-credentials grant for active service accounts. Supply grant_type=client_credentials, `client_id=<service-account UUID>`, and `client_secret=<full tfk_live_... or tfk_test_... service-account API key>`. Client credentials may instead be sent with HTTP Basic authentication. Tokens use the configured auth.jwtExpirySeconds capped at 900 seconds and carry the service account's current workspace role, effective permissions, and effective API scopes.

request.description:
List orders

Lists Basic orders using the same envelope as `GET /orders/{orderId}`. Required API-key scope: `orders_read`; a member session needs permission to view or place orders. Newest first by created time and id. A status filter is applied to stored order facts first and then to each order's canonical public status; a filtered page keeps reading until it holds limit items or the orders end, within a bounded scan. A bounded scan that stops before the orders end always answers a nextCursor, even on a page shorter than limit (or an empty one): follow nextCursor until it is null. A cursor is bound to the caller, workspace and exact filters; a malformed, foreign or deleted anchor is INVALID_CURSOR.

header.description: Makes a retry safe. Required for API keys (a missing key answers 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED); optional for signed-in members. 1 to 255 bytes, unique per order you mean to place; a UUID is a good choice. A retry with the same key and the same body, from the same credential's owner in the same workspace within 24 hours, returns the first answer and never places a second order. The same key with a different body answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; another principal's key answers 403 IDEMPOTENCY_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED. A retry that arrives while the first request is still running waits for it, and answers 409 ORDER_IN_PROGRESS (with Retry-After) if it is still running after 30 seconds. A retry after a first request that may or may not have taken effect (it stopped without an answer, or failed after it reached the venue) answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, with no Retry-After: retrying that key can never settle it, so read the orders back (GET /api/v1/orders, details.readTarget) and use a new key only once the order is not there. Refusals are not stored: after one, fix the request and send it again with the same key or a new one.
Signed-in sessions whose member turned on the check for orders: a step-up proof for purpose `order_placement` bound to this quote. Ignored for API keys.

request.description:
Place an order

Place an order by the id of a quote you hold (`{quoteId}` from POST /quotes). A Basic venue quote becomes a venue trade (`basicTrade`). Each quote is ordered once: the same quote again answers QUOTE_ALREADY_ORDERED, and a replay with the same Idempotency-Key and body returns the first answer. Read what a quote produced with `GET /orders/by-quote/{quoteId}`. A Live prices row is ordered directly with `{kind: "stream", priceId, minReceive | slippageBps}`: the priceId from GET /prices is checked for this workspace and its validFor before anything is sent (PRICE_ID_INVALID, PRICE_EXPIRED), then the venue is asked for that exact size and the order runs exactly as a quote order of that venue, with the same permission, order resource and outcome fields. Its limit is `minReceive`, or `slippageBps` below the price's receive amount (rounded up to the Asset's precision); a price outside it is refused with details.remediation `widenLimit`, details.currentReceive and details.requiredSlippageBps.

request.description:
Get an order

Returns the latest stored order after a provider refresh. For REST polling, wait 10–15 seconds between reads and honor `Retry-After` on 429; do not poll in a tight loop. After a webhook delivery, perform this GET to obtain the complete current projection. Never put an API key in a URL. Terminality is order-kind dependent: route and atomic venue orders normally complete at `settled`, while claim-based or deferred products may advance to `finalized`.

request.description:
Cancel an order

Cancels an undispatched Basic order or a pay-in still awaiting funds. Returns the same order envelope as GET, with status cancelled and terminal true. Repeating cancellation leaves the order unchanged. A durable dispatch claim, a progressed funding leg, or a terminal outcome refuses with ORDER_NOT_CANCELLABLE and details.status. Required API-key scope: `orders_write`, with an Idempotency-Key; a member session needs permission to place orders. No venue cancellation is attempted.

request.description:
Submit a step of an order

Answers a step of an order that trades from a wallet the client signs for itself: the order's `next` with `kind: sign`. The body is tagged by `kind`: `signedTransaction` (`raw`, for TetraFi to broadcast), `transactionHash` (`txHash` of the step's transaction the client broadcast), `signature` (a `typedData` step) or `declined`. Past the step's `signBy`, only `transactionHash` is still taken (a transaction the client broadcast itself, checked like any other); the other kinds refuse SIGNING_STEP_EXPIRED. A signed transaction must be legacy (EIP-155), EIP-2930 or EIP-1559 (else SIGNING_TRANSACTION_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED) and is checked against the step (`chainId`, `from`, `to`, `data`, `value`, `nonce`) before anything is sent; a difference refuses SIGNING_STEP_MISMATCH with details.field. Nothing is sent until the wallet's screening passed, and while the wallet no longer holds the token the trade spends or, for a signed transaction, its value and gas at the signed fee (SIGNING_WALLET_FUNDS_SHORT, details.field balance or gas). Answers the order envelope, the same as GET, once the order moved past the step (its next step to sign, or a terminal outcome); a request holds at most 15 s, after which the order answers `next: wait`. Every 503 names its cause in details.cause (screening, chainRead, relay or stepStore). A signed-in member answers the steps of their own orders (Place orders permission); an API key those of its own orders (scope `orders_write`). An Idempotency-Key is required; a replay answers the first answer and sends nothing again.

header.description: Makes a retry safe; optional. 1 to 255 bytes; a UUID is a good choice. A retry with the same key and the same body, from the same credential's owner in the same workspace within 24 hours, returns the first answer (header Idempotent-Replayed: true; its quotes may have expired since) and asks no venue again. The same key with a different body answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; a retry while the first is still running waits for its answer. Refusals are not stored. Not accepted with Accept: text/event-stream (400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID): a streamed answer cannot be replayed.

request.description:
Request quotes

Request a `PairQuoteSet` from eligible venues, or requote one held quote. Members need Request quotes; keys need `quotes_request` and `orders_write`. A venue ask is limited to one every three seconds per caller (`429 QUOTE_RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`). Guide: [search/how-it-works](https://tetrafi.mintlify.app/search/how-it-works).

A requote can ask a production desk for a firm price in `auto` mode. Firm venue-account quotes also require `workspace_venue_trade`, the venue enabled on the key and request signing; otherwise the card is indicative with `sourceRefusal: venueTradeScopeRequired`. A key has no default wallet: `source.tradingWallets` maps CAIP-2 networks to workspace custody or granted organisation financial-account IDs. Personal wallets refuse with `409 PERSONAL_TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED`. `deliverTo` is for member sessions; on a key requote it is `409 REQUOTE_REFUSED` (`details.reason: deliverToNotPermitted`). Refusals use `ApiError`.

request.description:
Read a quote request's recorded answer

The quotes, sources and orders of one asset-pair POST /quotes answer. Required API-key scope: `quotes_read`. Immediate reads use the same held request handed to the asynchronous evidence writer; later reads recover its durable record. Readable by the principal that asked, by a member session allowed to view the workspace's orders, and by an API key with the additional orders_read scope when an order was placed on one of its quotes in that workspace. Unknown and foreign ids are the same 404. A request lost in a crash before persistence returns 404 QUOTE_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND; its unpersisted quotes are also lost, so request fresh quotes. Genuine store or read failures return retryable 503 QUOTE_REQUEST_UNAVAILABLE with details.retryAfter and Retry-After. requestedByYou says whether the caller asked; only then can it order these quotes.

request.description:
Read balances across workspace accounts

Read cache-only balances across readable workspace wallets and venue accounts; no provider refresh starts. Keys and OAuth clients need `treasury_read`. Wallet policy must allow `read_balances`; venue accounts require View wallets in a company or broker workspace or as an admitted LP taker, as on the account balance read. Guide: [trade/balances](https://tetrafi.mintlify.app/trade/balances).

`network` is the CAIP-2 chain and an exact filter; unknown parameters are refused. `valueUsd` uses the market-data display price (up to eight decimals); `valuedAt` dates that price. Without a price both are null, never zero. `GET …/balances:aggregate` gives totals rounded to cents and daily history.

Sort with `field` or `-field`: `id` (default), `accountId`, `asset`, `network`, `valueUsd` (unvalued last) or `asOf`. `fields` restricts row fields but keeps `id`, `accountId` and `asset`; `include=account` adds the account by `accountId` as its resource answers it, or null with its refusal. Hidden accounts affect neither rows nor cursors. Cursors bind the workspace, caller, filters, sort and ordered visible row identities.

query.description: A CAIP-2 network (`eip155:8453`): only balances held on it.

`field` or `-field`, field one of `id` (the default), `accountId`, `asset`, `network`,
`valueUsd` (unvalued rows last either way) and `asOf`.

request.description:
Read the cross-venue settlement plan

A read-only snapshot of what is due across the workspace's venue accounts. Unknown deadlines remain unknown. Per-source read failures are explicit and make the plan incomplete. Reading creates no transfer, reservation, approval request or LP instruction. perspective=maker requires a human session in an LP workspace (otherwise 403 LP_WORKSPACE_REQUIRED) and lists only client windows covered by the current client-sharing grant. Turns are relative to that LP; clocks and SLA facts use the same native window projection. Client funding sources and executable proposals are never exposed. The plan is not paged: it returns every window of the horizon, and a horizon holding more than 512 windows is refused whole with 422 SETTLEMENT_PLAN_TOO_LARGE, never truncated (horizonDays is 1 to 90; send a shorter one). Required API-key scope: `settlements_read`; an OAuth client needs the same scope. The key's owner must also be allowed to view the workspace's settlements.

query.description: `taker` (default): this workspace's accounts. `maker`: the LP's granted clients' windows.

Only this venue account's windows, sources and summary (taker perspective). A venue account

request.description:
List trades

The one trade history. Projections: scope=workspace (default) reads the workspace's taker orders and venue trades; a caller not allowed to view the workspace's compliance records reads only their own, whatever the scope. scope=mine reads the caller's own (a member session only). scope=umbrella reads a broker's clients' orders with each client category's field visibility (a member session allowed to view client compliance records). perspective=maker reads an LP workspace's fills with pseudonymised counterparties (a member session allowed to view settlements); a member allowed to view orders or bilateral documents but not settlements reads order summaries instead (maker.summary, without tradeId: the LP's protocol orders, their status, route and recorded USD value); with settlementStage or minAgeSeconds, its unsettled orders by stage (a member session allowed to view bilateral documents). The default perspective is taker in every workspace. Every row except an order summary carries tradeId, kind (order or venueTrade) and projection. Page with limit and cursor; format=csv returns the same filtered rows. Required API-key scope: `trades_read`; CSV is a member session only.

The settlement milestones flow analytics records are its `milestones` sub-resource. Each perspective answers exactly what its own route answers.

request.description:
List venue-account credit

List recorded credit for accounts that settle through a venue account. Requires View wallets and View credit, plus `treasury_read` for keys and OAuth. Accounts are admitted by stored row and venue kind and read concurrently. Guide: [trade/settlement-and-credit#monitor-credit-per-account](https://tetrafi.mintlify.app/trade/settlement-and-credit#monitor-credit-per-account).

An item's `unreachable` reason can be `VENUE_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND` for an unowned account, `VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDS_IN_WALLETS` for a wallet-based venue, or a 503 of the item read. Each readable item's components name a missing key or `VENUE_ACCOUNT_KEY_STATE_UNAVAILABLE` if key state could not be read. `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, `INVALID_LIMIT` or `INVALID_CURSOR` names bad input; missing credit permission is `403 INSUFFICIENT_WORKSPACE_PERMISSION`. An unreadable account list refuses with 503.

Only these venue accounts, comma-separated (any of, at most 100). Without it, every venue
account of the workspace that settles through a venue account.

`consumers` expands every listed account's commitment rows under the page's
`included.consumers[venueAccountId]`, as on the item read.
Page size, 1 to 100 (default 20); any other value is 400 INVALID_LIMIT.
The `nextCursor` of the previous page of this list.

request.description:
Read the venue account's balances at its venue

The caller must be allowed to view wallets in a company or broker workspace (or be an admitted LP taker). API keys and OAuth clients additionally require treasury_read; this read never authorizes a payment. Read through the connection holding the account's balance credential, a configured one first (its `connectionId` and execution type are in the body); the observation, staleness and display-value rules are those of the venue-connection balance read, so a balance key held only by a disabled venue returns its last-known balance. 409 VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDS_IN_WALLETS for an account whose money is in the company's own wallets, VENUE_ACCOUNT_REVERIFY_REQUIRED when no current key holds its balance, VENUE_ACCOUNT_REVOKED for a disconnected account, VENUE_ACCOUNT_VENUE_UNKNOWN when its venue is not recognised; 404 VENUE_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND. 403 VENUE_READ_AUTHORITY_REFUSED whenever the caller's read authority has ended, whether the check before the read or a recheck during it sees it (reason `authority_ended`: the credential is revoked or expired, or no longer carries treasury_read; reason `permission_withdrawn`: its owner lost permission to view wallets, its membership or taker admission); a session that has itself ended answers 401.

request.description:
Read one venue account's credit

Read the Treasury credit card for one account without calling the provider. Requires View wallets and View credit, plus `treasury_read` for keys and OAuth. A signed-in member can use the account ledger for a live read. Guide: [trade/settlement-and-credit#credit-and-the-ledger](https://tetrafi.mintlify.app/trade/settlement-and-credit#credit-and-the-ledger).

`warning` is the workspace threshold as a percent of reported limit, or null if unset. `warningReached` requires a readable line; `revision` is the PATCH ETag. Usage comes from the credit admission owner, including holds, freshness and terms provenance. `include=consumers` expands `included.consumers[venueAccountId].value`: `unsettledLeg`/`windowId`, `openTrade`/`tradeId`, or `openQuote`/`quoteId`, each with asset, exact decimal amount and `since`. It shares the commitments' snapshot and sums to them per asset. Unreadable expansion is null with a named reason. Failed terms reads refuse with 503, never an invented version. Foreign accounts share `404 VENUE_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND`; unreadable account access is `503 VENUE_ACCOUNT_ELIGIBILITY_UNAVAILABLE`.

request.description:
Read the venue account's deposit history

Read credits through the configured balance-key connection, using its deposit-history rules. Requires View wallets in a company or broker workspace or as an admitted LP taker, plus `treasury_read` for keys and OAuth. Unread history is named in `unreachable`, not an empty history. Guide: [trade/balances](https://tetrafi.mintlify.app/trade/balances).

Credits sort by venue record time then venue deposit id. A cursor overrides `from` and binds the workspace, account, asset, network and full credit fingerprint; a changed observation refuses it rather than skipping or repeating credits. An unread history's source is `depositHistory`; `reason` and `readAt` come from the observation's `reasonCode` and `observedAt` (when read). The included observation also names connection, reason code, asset, `chainRef`, `networkCode`, `networkConfirmed`, `observedAt` and `expiresAt`. With no venue network declaration, `networkConfirmed` is false, `networkCode` empty and matching is by asset only.

`400 INVALID_REQUEST` names an unknown parameter or out-of-range `from`. The balance read's 409s apply, plus `VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDING_VENUE_DISABLED` if only a disabled venue holds the balance key. `403 VENUE_READ_AUTHORITY_REFUSED` covers authority lost before or during the read: `authority_ended` for revoked, expired or rescoped credentials, `permission_withdrawn` for lost View wallets, membership or taker admission. An ended session answers 401.

request.description:
Read how to deposit into the venue account

Read deposit instructions through the configured balance-key connection. Requires View wallets in a company or broker workspace or as an admitted LP taker, plus `treasury_read` for keys. This does not authorize a payment. Guide: [trade/balances](https://tetrafi.mintlify.app/trade/balances).

Select `currency` for bank details. `bankDeposit` names `available`, `referenceOnly`, `notOffered` or `unread` with reason and code. `bankInstructions` carries the available coordinates or reference. Only a declared venue offering determines `notOffered`; failed reads are `unread`. Responses are `no-store`; receiving-account and full-reference disclosures are audited. Connection selection and fee rules apply.

Send a summary pay-in window's `payInLegId` alone (`400 PAY_IN_LEG_SELECTION_EXCLUSIVE`) for that open leg's currency and the linked paying bank recorded on its deposit declaration at a dedicated fiat venue. Wrong account or leg: `404 PAY_IN_LEG_NOT_FOUND`; no longer awaiting funds: `409 PAY_IN_LEG_NOT_OPEN`; digital asset: `409 PAY_IN_LEG_NOT_BANK_CURRENCY` (read its address with `asset` and `chainRef`). The balance read's 409s apply, plus `VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDING_VENUE_DISABLED` if only a disabled venue holds the key, before leg lookup.

`403 VENUE_READ_AUTHORITY_REFUSED` covers authority lost before or during the read: `authority_ended` for revoked, expired or rescoped credentials, `permission_withdrawn` for lost View wallets, membership or taker admission. An ended session answers 401.

query.description: The CAIP-2 network to deposit `asset` on.
ISO fiat currency for the bank-deposit read; never with `asset` or `network`.
The dedicated fiat venue's linked bank id for the sending bank. Required with currency for a dedicated fiat venue and refused for other venues.

One of the venue account's open pay-in legs (a summary pay-in window's `legId`):
the read selects that leg's currency and, for a dedicated fiat venue, the paying
bank its deposit declaration recorded. Only on the venue-account read, and never
with `asset`, `network`, `currency` or `providerBankId`.

Deposits to and withdrawals from the venue account that settle obligations, newest first, optionally for one window; page with cursor. Required API-key scope: `settlements_read`; an OAuth client needs the same scope. The key's owner must also be allowed to view the workspace's settlements.

request.description:
List the workspace's venue accounts

List venue accounts for a current company or broker session, or a key or service account with `treasury_read` and View wallets authority. Guide: [trade/wallets-and-accounts](https://tetrafi.mintlify.app/trade/wallets-and-accounts).

Items carry the venue, funds location, wallets, linked accounts, execution types, key state and whether disabling the venue retires its key. An account-based item's `accountId` is the `venueAccountId` for balances, deposit history and instructions; a `walletBased` item has no account or `accountId`, and `fundingTarget` names its organisation trading wallets. Key by `venueEnablementId`. Oldest first; `limit` defaults to 20, max 100. Pass the opaque `nextCursor` as `cursor` until null.

An unknown or foreign workspace is `404 WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND`, without reading that workspace. A cursor this list did not issue is `400 INVALID_CURSOR`. `403 VENUE_READ_AUTHORITY_REFUSED` names `authority_ended` for revoked, expired or rescoped credentials or `permission_withdrawn` for lost View wallets, membership or taker admission. An ended session answers 401.

request.description:
List the workspace's wallets being created

The wallets created on a wallet connection, newest first, each with its status and the people who have not proven their factors yet (`missing`). `status=pending` lists the pending wallets; a pending wallet past its expiry reads as `expired`. `assignee=me` lists only the wallets waiting for you: your factors to prove while pending, or the created wallet's owners to confirm from your own signing page while `created` or `active` (each with its `signingRequestId`); never one you confirmed or that does not name you. It also lists a registered organisation wallet you created whose Trade grant, chosen at creation, is not written yet (`creatorTradeGrant`): `POST …/wallets/{walletId}/reconcile` in your own session writes it. A personal wallet is listed to its creator only; an organisation wallet to its people and to members with ManageWallets. Workspace membership is enough to read the wallets that name you (an invitation to prove your factors); `createdBy` names who started each. Registered custody wallets are read from wallet-directory. A member's API key with `treasury_read` reads the wallets its member would, as that member's permissions stand now.

query.description: Comma-separated statuses (`pending`, `creating`, `uncertain`, `created`, `active`, `readbackMismatch`, `failed`, `expired`).

`me`: only the wallets with your own signing request open (factors to prove
while pending, or the created wallet's owners to confirm), at any status.

Related objects to expand into `included`, comma-separated, each keyed by the wallets' `connectionId`. `connection`: the wallet's connection exactly as `GET …/wallet-providers/setup-connections` lists it to this caller, or null with that list's refusal (403 without View wallets, 403 `JWT_REQUIRED` for an API key) or 404 `WALLET_CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND` for a connection the workspace no longer has. `capabilities`: its capability report exactly as `GET …/wallet-providers/connections/{connectionId}/capabilities` answers this caller, or null with that read's refusal. Unknown relation 400 `INCLUDE_UNKNOWN`, malformed or repeated 400 `INCLUDE_INVALID`; not on a signed API-key request.

request.description:
Create a wallet

Start an organisation wallet with `treasury_write` and Manage wallets, or the key member's personal wallet with `orders_write` and View wallets. The member's current permissions and standing apply. The key never approves. Guide: [trade/create-wallet](https://tetrafi.mintlify.app/trade/create-wallet).

Connection capabilities, threshold and each owner's current membership are checked before recording anything. `202` includes the signing request's `id`; the approval link is also `wallet.approvalUrl`. A key receives no approval capability. Another owner on a personal creation is `409 WALLET_CREATION_PERSONAL_OWNER`. `startedWithApiKey` names the initiating key. The same `Idempotency-Key` and body make one creation; a different body with the same key is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`.

`returnUrl` must be HTTPS on a registered exact origin (scheme, host and port), excluding TetraFi's app and signing origins; otherwise `400 RETURN_URL_NOT_REGISTERED`. `returnTo` echoes it. The query outcome is `approved` or `pending` immediately after recording the owner's part (`pending` while waiting for others), or `refused` only after they see why and choose to return.

Listed to the same people as the list: a personal wallet to its creator, an organisation wallet to its people and to members with ManageWallets; any other id is 404 `WALLET_NOT_FOUND`. request.description:
Withdraw a wallet being created

Withdraws a wallet being created, saying what is known at its provider. A `pending` creation (nothing sent yet) is withdrawn at once and reads `cancelled` with `failureCode` `WALLET_CREATION_CANCELLED`. An `uncertain` one is read again first: one the provider holds, or one still inside its settle window, is refused by name (`WALLET_CREATION_EXISTS_AT_PROVIDER`, `WALLET_CREATION_ACTIVITY_EXISTS`, `WALLET_CREATION_ABSENCE_UNPROVEN`); a failed read withdraws nothing (`503 WALLET_CREATION_CANCEL_UNAVAILABLE`). Any other status is `409 WALLET_CREATION_NOT_CANCELLABLE`. A member's own API key may withdraw what its member could, with the scope its creation needed: `orders_write` for a personal wallet, `treasury_write` for an organisation wallet (`403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` otherwise, `details.requiredScope` naming the one it needs). A key holding neither scope is refused before its body is read, and that refusal's `details.requiredScope` names `orders_write`, the first of the two. `Idempotency-Key` is required: the same key replays the withdrawal.

Standard Webhooks sends webhook-id, webhook-timestamp (Unix seconds), and webhook-signature: `v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256>`, signing id.timestamp.rawBody with the base64-decoded key. Verify the exact raw body and enforce five-minute timestamp tolerance. Required API-key scope: `webhooks_manage`; the key's owner must still be allowed to manage webhooks. request.description:
Send a test delivery

Trigger a webhook.test delivery signed with the same Standard Webhooks headers (webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature) as live events. Required API-key scope: `webhooks_manage`; the key's owner must still be allowed to manage webhooks. A member session needs permission to manage webhooks or credentials.

request.description:
Resume a paused webhook

Reactivate an auto-paused webhook, resetting its failure count and pause time. Required API-key scope: `webhooks_manage`; the key's owner must still be allowed to manage webhooks. A member session needs permission to manage webhooks or credentials.

request.description:
Rotate a webhook secret

Rotate a webhook's Standard Webhooks secret. Returns a shown-once `whsec_<base64>` secret. For 24 hours, webhook-signature carries space-separated `v1,<base64>` signatures from current and previous decoded keys; either verifies id.timestamp.rawBody. Required API-key scope: `webhooks_manage`; the key's owner must still be allowed to manage webhooks. A member session needs permission to manage webhooks or credentials.
